placements.why: The envelope's entire content is an instrument-calibration report (Kestrelwood spectrograph tuned to 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates). Existing strata is empty in this repo, but 'Calibration' is named verbatim in the org's own taxonomy (Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates/Calibration) — an EXACT match for the organizational category this content belongs under, simply not yet instantiated. Minting it here (rather than forcing the content under an unrelated stratum) follows the rule that strata grows one real mint at a time from actual content.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as its own operational domain, not folded into another stratum
placements.frame: What instrument or measurement apparatus is being calibrated, against what reference standard, and does that calibration hold across its full claimed range?

placements.title: Calibration status is established by verification against a named reference standard, not by assertion alone
placements.frame: What reference standard or plates was the calibration checked against, and does the confirmed range or band match what was claimed?
placements.why: Both segments trace one directional theme in flat technical register: a stated calibration result (src-1) substantiated by an explicit verification procedure against the June reference plates, holding across the full observing band (src-2). This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (new instruments, new frequencies, new reference checks) — not a one-time fact — so it passes the narrative grain test. No existing leaf or strata exists in this repo to reuse (both supplied structures are empty), so mint is required; nothing closer than the newly-minted Calibration strata itself exists to set as lineage, so no lineage edge is set.
